newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan to sell cheap cars on internet in '97.
newsitem.headline: Nissan to sell cheap cars on internet in '97.

text.p: Japan's Nissan Motor Co will start selling cheaper passenger cars on the internet from next summer, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Saturday.
Internet users will be able buy a car from the comfort of home from electronic catalogues on Nissan's homepages to be launched by the middle of next year, the daily reported.

The Japanese motor giant will advertise 'internet car' models, modified variants of existing models for sale exclusively on the internet, which is accessible with a common home computer, the Nihon Keizai reported.

Nissan aims to sell internet cars cheaper by cutting promotion costs, such as advertising and marketing. The company's car homepages will feature full colour images and detailed information on the models on sale and will offer an electronic mail information service.
Nissan is the first Japanese car manufacturer to launch internet car sales but is expected to be soon followed by other domestic motor giants, the business daily reported.
The car maker will further cut costs by linking its headquarters to dealers with a recently created computer network.
